collection_method: Read-only GitHub repository, issue-search, issue and comment GET requests through the GitHub connector. Embedded code and reproductions were treated as evidence and not executed. No packages, agents, models, tools, pipelines, workflows or target systems were run or contacted.

selected_records.title: BUG: Managed agents share state causing identical parallel execution results
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported shared child-agent state collapsed parallel delegated tasks and returned only one observation
selected_records.provider_attribution: A configured smolagents manager and one reused managed-agent instance; the reporter used an OpenAI model, but the defect is attributed to shared framework state rather than provider behavior.
selected_records.assessment: The manager requested three different tasks in one step, received only one child observation and retried the missing tasks. This preserves result transfer and downstream reaction, but the apparent participants are repeated calls to one intentionally configured child instance, not independently authenticated agents or a rogue swarm.

selected_records.title: BUG: ManagedAgent provide_run_summary leaks inner tool calls and responses into parent observation
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled summary boundary leaked child tool transcripts into the parent observation
selected_records.provider_attribution: smolagents managed-agent summary path with a deterministic local stub; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A keyless deterministic reproduction shows child tool calls and responses entering the parent observation despite summary mode. This is a concrete cross-agent information transfer into recipient context, but it occurs in a designed parent-child workflow and does not show autonomous intent or a novel real-world episode.

selected_records.title: ManagedAgent swallows tool errors from sub-agents - manager sees empty/None result
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: reported failure provenance lost at the managed-agent boundary
selected_records.provider_attribution: smolagents manager/sub-agent wrapper; the example names a hosted model, but no provider-side cause is established.
selected_records.assessment: The public report says tool errors or step exhaustion become an empty result, after which the manager can retry or proceed on a false assumption. This is a transfer-contract failure in an intentional hierarchy, not evidence of independently acting participants.

selected_records.title: human_in_the_loop: duplicate tool-call-name ambiguity guard silently skipped, causing wrong decisions to be applied
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled mixed-ID test applied a human decision to the wrong same-name tool call
selected_records.provider_attribution: Haystack human-in-the-loop decision binding; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: The reporter explicitly says this was a latent audit finding, not a live pipeline incident, and that ordinary generators do not emit the mixed identifier shape. It is a useful authorization-binding control but not an observed agent exchange.

selected_records.title: Agent tool scheduler picks write-write winner by batch order, not call order, contradicting its own docstring and #11690
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled scheduler merged concurrent tool state in dependency-batch rather than requested call order
selected_records.provider_attribution: Haystack Agent tool scheduler with deterministic local functions; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic three-tool test shows a later dependency batch overwriting the state winner promised by call order. The record closed after a proposed fix discussion. It concerns configured tools and shared state, not distinguishable autonomous participants.

selected_records.title: HITL: ToolExecutionDecision(execute=True) without final_tool_params runs the tool with empty parameters and reports a user modification
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: controlled custom approval strategy caused different default parameters to execute
selected_records.provider_attribution: Haystack custom human-in-the-loop strategy with a scripted generator; no model-provider execution.
selected_records.assessment: A deterministic test shows an approval object with omitted final parameters can execute tool defaults and insert a false modification message. A maintainer closed the issue as documented optionality applying only to denial or parameterless tools, so this remains a contract/dispute control rather than a confirmed supported-path bypass or swarm event.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The strongest records preserve child-result transfer into a manager, raw child tool output entering a parent context and manager reaction to collapsed parallel results, but all are previously published failures inside intentionally configured frameworks.
limitations: Searches were capped at 30 newest-updated rows and overlap; this is not a complete issue census.
Issue bodies and comments are public tracker evidence, not authenticated agent telemetry.
Configured managers, managed agents, tools and pipelines are not independently verified autonomous participants.
Open issue state or later comments do not establish continuing agent activity.
No code, package, reproduction, agent, model, tool, pipeline, workflow or target service was executed or contacted.

Advancement requires an unpublished original real-run exchange with independently corroborated autonomous participants, transferred task work actually used by a distinguishable recipient, and evidence that the coordination itself crossed operator authorization rather than reflecting shared instance state, summary behavior, error handling, approval binding or scheduler merges.
redactions: No executable reproduction bodies, example secret values, personal addresses, private logs or tool payloads are included.
Assessments retain public record links, timestamps and body hashes while summarizing mechanisms at a domain level.
